ANNUAL REPORT 2022
MESSAGE 2022
Dear valued customers, partners and shareholders,
In 2022, the confluence of multiple crises including heightened 
geopolitical conflict, surging global inflation and severe 
consequences of the Covid-19 pandemic battered the 
global economy with the prospects of recession. Despite 
the unprecedented headwinds in 2022, Vietnam’s economy 
recorded positive outcomes after 2 years of fighting against 
the pandemic and promoting economic recovery: GDP grew 
at 8.02%; average CPI was kept under controlled at 3.15%; 
trade surplus reached USD11.2 billion. Vietnam was also the 
only country in the Asia-Pacific and among few countries 
in the world with credit rating being improved in the year. 
Contributing to this success, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) 
actively and flexibly managed and deployed a multiplicity of 
monetary policy instruments, interest rates and exchange rate 
policies. The result was that inflationary pressure was tamed, 
macro-economy was stable and the economy was resilient.
Proud journey, high aspiration
2022 was a significant year for BIDV since it celebrated 65 years 
of growth and development. Despite the numerous obstacles 
and challenges facing the economy, with the leadership by the 
Government, the State Bank, close companionship of partners 
and customers, and the concerted efforts of all employees, 
BIDV comprehensively completed and exceeded the goals 
of its Master Development Strategy till 2025, with vision to 
2030 and the 2022 business plan as approved by the General 
Meeting of Shareholders. The Bank continues to cement its 
position as the leading financial institution in the country. 
At the end of 2022, BIDV was the first commercial bank 
with total assets exceeding VND2 quadrillion, an increase of 
20.4% from 2021, and continued to maintain its position as 
the largest joint stock commercial bank in Vietnam. Capital 
mobilized from organizations and individuals rose 8.4% to 
VND1.64 quadrillion, making up approximately 14% of the 
deposit market share of the banking sector. Outstanding loans 
reached VND1.53 quadrillion, up 12.1%, accounting for 12.87% 
of total outstanding loans of the whole economy, leading by 
market share within the sector. Loan structure shifted towards 
sustainability, the proportion of retail loans reached 43.4%, an 
increase of 3.6% compared to the beginning of the year, the 
proportion of outstanding loans of SME reached 22%...
Credit quality was controlled within limits, non-performing 
loan ratio was 0.96%. Business performance improved 
compared to the same period last year, exceeding the goals 
set in the 2022 plan: (i) Net operating income before credit 
losses reached VND47,045 billion. Consolidated pre-tax profit 
grew 69.8% to VND23,009 billion, exceeding the plan set by 
the General Meeting of Shareholders; (ii) Financial capacity 
improved with chartered capital reaching VND50,585 billion; 
market capitalization was among the market leaders, reaching 
VND195.3 trillion (~USD8.34 billion); (iii) Profitability indicators 
improved positively compared to the previous year: ROA was 
0.95%; ROE was 19.34%; (iv) Provisions for credit risks were 
fully made according to regulations; non-performing loan 
coverage ratio reached 226%, capital adequacy ratio followed 
regulations and good practices. BIDV was one of the banks 
with the largest contributions to the state budget, reaching 
over VND6.7 trillion in 2022.
In 2022, BIDV also made significant advancements in 
institutional development and corporate governance. The 
bank completed the organizational structure and model of 
a modern bank, improving human resources at all levels by 
implementing BIDV Leaders Development Program at the 
age of 30, developing a regulation on job titles and career 
development. BIDV has adhered to the objectives of the 
Overall Business Strategy for the years 2021–2025 and 07 
Component Strategies through regular assessment and in-
depth examination, thus taking key solutions according to the 
direction. 
BIDV pursues the “green banking” approach and recognizes 
it as one of the key priorities for the foreseeable future. BIDV 
is currently the market leader in green financing, helping to 
shift the economy toward green growth and environmental 
protection by focusing on developing and implementing a 
Governance Framework, ESG business model (environmental, 
social, and governance), enforcing policies and regulations, 
developing unique products and services, and adjusting the 
structure and organizational model towards green banking. In 
addition, as a major commercial bank, BIDV has proactively 
adopted solutions to resolve difficulties, support clients, and 
promote business and production activities.
BIDV proactively implemented social security programs to 
support the fight against the Covid-19 pandemic, as well as 
initiatives to aid in education, national security, health, and 
community development... This year also celebrated the 
accomplishment of the strategic partnership between BIDV 
Securities Company (BSC) and Hana Securities; the complete 
and extended strategic cooperation between BIDV and Hana 
Financial Group has reached a new level.
With the successful outcomes, BIDV’s reputation and brand 
were further upheld; Both domestically and abroad, the 
confidence of partners and clients continued to grow: The 
issuer rating and deposit (local/foreign currency) rating of 
BIDV were raised by Moody’s from Ba3 to Ba2; BIDV has been 
named “Best Retail Bank in Vietnam 2022” (The Asian Banker), 
“Best Bank for Corporate Customers in Southeast Asia in 2022” 
(Global Banking and Finance), “Vietnam Domestic FDI Bank 
of the Year 2022”, “Best Bank Providing Foreign Exchange 
and Derivatives Services in Vietnam” (ABF Wholesale 
Banking Awards), “Most Innovative Risk Management Bank 
in 2022” (International Business Magazine); Top 10 prestigious 
Vietnamese commercial banks 2022 (Vietnam Report)… 
Pioneering, developing together
Entering 2023, BIDV carries a proactive attitude and great 
determination to sprint to the finish line, effectively achieving 
the objective of the entire 2021–2025 period. “Discipline 
- Efficiency – Operational Transformation” is the BIDV’s 
action motto for 2023. BIDV will continue to expand its 
operational scope while managing risk, increasing efficiency, 
and shifting structure towards optimizing risk assets. Credit 
quality will be strictly controlled and asset quality improved; 
Increase operational effectiveness in association with income 
restructuring in order to boost non-interest income; Integrate 
digital transformation solutions simultaneously and accelerate 
the execution of important IT projects; Increase the capacity 
for corporate governance and risk management, proactive 
response to the financial market’s unpredictable volatility; 
Concentrate on capital raising plans to strengthen financial 
capacity and business development. Additionally, as the largest 
green lender in Vietnam in accordance with the Government’s 
orientation, BIDV has established core strategies and activities 
for the future to focus resources on green development, 
financial sustainability, and improving ESG practices. 
65 years of construction and development is a proud journey 
fostered by generations of BIDV leaders and staff who have 
overcome challenges to shape a resilient BIDV. At this point, 
with the determination of the leadership, the cooperation 
and consensus of the employees, BIDV has set the goals 
to reach new heights. Built on the precious historic values, 
the brand identity of BIDV has been changed to reflect the 
colors of “5-pointed golden star, apricot flower and emerald 
green”. According to Eastern philosophy, number 5 represents 
fertility, vitality, and lasting harmony; symbolizing 5 continents 
- expressing the desire for integration; the emerald green 
symbolizes sustainability and longevity, bearing the image of a 
“green” bank, as the strategy that BIDV is determined to pursue.
On behalf of the Board of Directors of BIDV, I would like to 
express my sincere thanks to the leadership and 28,000 
employees of the Bank. My sincere thanks also go to all of the 
clients, investors, and partners who have trusted and supported 
BIDV over the years. I look forward to receiving your continued 
support in the coming time so that we can create sustainable 
values for a thriving future.
I wish you continued growth and success! 
Yours sincerely,
                     ON BEHALF OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
                                                 CHAIRMAN
	
	
          Phan Duc Tu

BIDV OVERVIEW 2022
BIDV was established on 26 April 1957 under the 
Prime Minister’s Decree No. 177/TTg. Over 65 years of 
establishment and development, with different names 
and tasks suitable to the requirements of each national 
development phase: Bank for Construction of Vietnam 
(1957-1981); Bank for Investment and Construction 
of Vietnam (1981-1990); Bank for Investment and 
Development of Vietnam (1990-2012); Joint Stock 
Commercial Bank for Investment and Development of 
Vietnam (since 1 May 2012), BIDV has always successfully 
completed all tasks assigned.
After 65 years of operations with more than 27 years of 
commercial operation, until now, BIDV has become a 
modern multi-owned financial institution operating in 
different countries in diverse business areas, with open and 
transparent operations following international governance 
practices... BIDV currently has a comprehensive ecosystem 
of banking - insurance - securities - financial investment 
and a wide network of 1,085 branches and transaction 
offices domestically and internationally, 11 subsidiaries 
and commercial presences in Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar, 
Russia, Taiwan (China); more than 28,000 well-trained and 
experienced employees, more than 15 million individual 
customers and 500,000 corporate customers, has 
established relationships with 2,300 financial institutions 
in 178 countries and territories. BIDV is currently the largest 
commercial bank by assets in Vietnam’s banking system. 
The State capital in BIDV has been secured and constantly 
developed. For consecutive years, BIDV has been one of 
the largest taxpayers in Vietnam.
Recognizing the great efforts of generations of BIDV 
employees during its 65-year history, the Party and 
State of Vietnam have awarded BIDV many noble titles 
and awards such as the Labor Hero in the Innovation 
Period, Ho Chi Minh Medal, Independence Medal, Labor 
Medals of all classes; the Lao PDR has awarded BIDV the 
Order of Independence, the Order of Labor, the Order of 
Friendship; The King of Cambodia awarded the Royal 
Order, the Order of Merit... On the occasion of its 65th 
anniversary, BIDV continued to be honored with noble 
awards including Third-Class Labor Medal of the Socialist 
Republic of Vietnam; Second-Class Development Medal 
of the Lao PDR; Moha Sena-Class Sahametrei Order of 
the King of Cambodia.
On 26 April 2022, BIDV turned 65 - a proud milestone in the glorious 
journey of a large commercial bank with the longest history in Vietnam’s 
banking system.

The Board of Directors, the Board of 
Management and all BIDV employees need 
to continue to inherit the achievements over 
the past 65 years and promote the stance 
and spirit of innovation to build a strong, safe, 
efficient and sustainable BIDV in the coming 
time, deserving its role as a key and market-
leading commercial bank in the Vietnam’s 
banking system.
On the occasion of the 65th anniversary, BIDV announced changes to its brand identity with effect from 26 April 
2022.
Over 65 years of operation and development, 
with comprehensive operations covering 
banking, insurance, securities, and financial 
investment, BIDV has become a leading 
commercial bank in Vietnam in terms of 
scale, quality, efficiency, financial capacity, 
institutional development, and is one of the 
pioneers in effectively implementing policies 
of the Party and State.
H.E. Mr. LE MINH KHAI 
Deputy Prime Minister
Addressing BIDV’s 65th anniversary, Mr. Le Minh Khai – 
Vietnam’s Deputy Prime Minister - praised BIDV’s great 
efforts, excellent achievements and positive contributions 
to the country’s development. The Deputy Prime Minister 
believed that in the coming time BIDV will continue to 
promote the tradition and great achievements of the past 
65 years, focusing on addressing limitations, overcoming 
difficulties and challenges, striving to successfully 
complete assigned tasks, growing strongly in all aspects, 
making more contributions to the national construction 
and defense.
Mrs. Nguyen Thi Hong - Governor of the State Bank of 
Vietnam - acknowledged and spoke highly of the proud 
achievements that BIDV’s generations have built over 
the years. The Governor specified tasks that BIDV must 
focus on in the coming time, including: implementing 
the Business Development Strategy for the 2021 – 2025 
period, joining the banking system to complete the 
Vietnam’s banking sector strategy until 2025, with vision 
to 2030; strengthening the system governance capacity 
according to practices; and improving credit quality; 
innovating and applying high technology to banking 
operations; improving financial capacity...
With the achievements and tradition fostered over the 
past 65 years, the intelligence, solidarity and creativity 
of generations of leaders and employees; the financial 
capacity, technology and high quality human resources, 
and the opportunities of the Industry 4.0, BIDV is 
determined to implement drastically and effectively 
policies of the Party and State, successfully fulfilling the 
tasks entrusted by the Party, State and the banking 
industry, actively contributing to the innovation, socio-
economic development and international integration of 
the country.
H.E. Madam NGUYEN THI HONG

BIDV would like to note the following risk factors that may affect the bank’s business 
performance.
In 2022, the economic environment had unfavorable 
developments, affecting the Vietnamese economy 
in general and BIDV’s operations in particular. 
Accordingly, the world economic growth slowed down 
due to unexpected shocks: (i) the Russia-Ukraine 
conflict since the end of February 2022 which has 
been persistent, predictable and showed no sign of 
ending; (ii) the re-emerging outbreak of the Covid-19 
pandemic and China’s strict disease control policy; 
(iii) Central banks of countries such as the US, Europe, 
the UK… hiked interest rates quickly to tame inflation; 
(iv) increased financial-monetary risks, food security, 
energy security and supply chain risks.
In 2022, despite having achieved the highest growth 
rate since 2011 (8.02%), and inflation was controlled at 
3.15% (better than the Government’s target of about 
4%), Vietnam’s economy faced major difficulties and 
challenges such as: (i) external risks and challenges 
with more obvious negative impacts as mentioned 
above; (ii) disbursement of public investment, national 
target programs and socio-economic development 
and recovery program 2022-2023 was still slow 
despite some improvement; (iii) inflation pressure, 
increased exchange rate and high interest rate were 
big challenges for 2022 and Q1-2023; (iv) potential 
bad debt. The increase in bad debt given the limited 
monetary policy room (rising inflation and high interest 
rates) will be a lingering challenge for credit institutions 
and the economy in 2023; (v) Some economic growth 
drivers such as export, investment, production, etc. 
signaled to slow down in the last months of 2022 
as business conditions deteriorated and the world 
demand declined sharply.
In 2022, given the risks from the international and 
domestic environment, BIDV was proactive, analyzed, 
timely assessed and developed flexible and specific 
scenarios to respond to the rapid and unusual 
movements of the market on the basis of compliance 
with regulatory policies of the Government, the State 
Bank and competent authorities; thereby, BIDV’s 
operations have always been safe, smooth and 
efficient.
In 2023, risks and challenges from the international 
context are forecast to remain such as: (i) The Covid-19 
pandemic and other diseases are still complicated 
and unpredictable; (ii) Geopolitical risk and strategic 
competition among major countries which continues 
to affect the global production and supply chains; (iii) 
Due to high interest rates, global economic growth 
of 2023 is forecast to decrease to about 12.8% from 
3.4% in 2022. In which, the US economy grows by 
1.6%, the EU by about 0.8% (some major economies of 
the region are likely to fall into a technical recession), 
China’s economy is forecast to recover but still grow 
slowly in 2023 (about 5.2%) even though the country 
has reopened since the start of the year; (iv) Although 
inflation has cooled down (after peaking in the third 
quarter of 2022), it is still forecast to be high in 2023 
(global CPI is about 7.0% in 2023, down from 8.7% in 
2022, according to IMF, April 2023) , forcing central 
banks of countries to increase interest rates (at least 
until the second quarter of 2023) and keep them at a 
high level in 2023. It also puts pressure on interest rates, 
exchange rates, financial risks (public debt, corporate 
and household debt, financial market liquidity, etc.) 
and other macroeconomic balances; and (v) Natural 
disasters, floods, and extreme climate change affect 
economic recovery in many countries and regions.
Intrinsic difficulties of Vietnam’s economy: (i) The 
international environment is less favorable; some 
regions and countries, especially Vietnam’s major 
trading partners, are likely to fall into a slight recession, 
which will reduce the demand for international exports, 
investment, consumption and international tourism; 
(ii) Disbursement of public investment, national 
target programs and socio-economic development 
and recovery program 2022-2023 are still slow; (iii) 
Increasing inflation pressure while interest rates are 
still high; (iv) Potential bad debt is likely to increase 
due to more difficult economic and business contexts; 
(v) Risks of corporate bonds, stock market, real estate... 
still exist and the liquidity of the banking system 
needs time to improve; and (vi) The labor market has 
improved but still faced uncertainties. Accordingly, 
Vietnam’s economy is forecast to have a lower growth 
(about 6-6.5 percent under the base scenario) and 
higher inflation (about 4-4.5 percent) in 2023.
The international and domestic economic outlooks 
show mixed opportunities and challenges, with 
difficulties and challenges being greater. BIDV 
is determined to complete its business plan with 
the motto “Discipline - Efficiency – Operational 
Transformation”, strictly following the orientation by 
the Government and the State Bank, ensuring the BIDV 
system to operate smoothly and safely, contributing 
to the development of the banking system and the 
national economy.

Law on Public-Private Partnership No.64/2020/QH14; 
Law on Tax management No.38/2019/QH14; Law

amending a number of articles of Law on State Audit. 
Law No.03/2022/QH15 amending and supplementing 
a number of articles of the Law on Public Investment, 
the Law on Public-Private Partnership, the Law 
on Investment, Law on Housing, Law on Bidding, 
Law on Electricity, the Law on Enterprises, Law on 
Special Consumption Tax and Law on Enforcement 
of Civil Judgments. The newly issued regulations were 
evaluated to be practical, suitable with the changes 
of the current business environment and have created 
fundamental changes in the operations of businesses 
in general and BIDV in particular.
Regarding 
bad 
debt 
settlement, 
the 
National 
Assembly 
issued 
Resolution 
No.

regarding extending the effective period of Resolution 
No. 42/2017/QH14 (“Resolution 42”) on piloting the 
settlement of bad debts of credit institutions to the end 
of 31 December 2023. This helped credit institutions, 
including BIDV to continue to apply Resolution 42 in 
order to speed up the process of handling bad debts, 
disposal of collateral in the banking system, and 
ensuring operational safety of the banking system 
in particular and the economy in general. However, 
there are many bad debts that are not covered by 
Resolution 42 (arising after 15 August 2017). Meanwhile, 
2015 Civil Code, Decree No. 21/2021/ND-CP dated 19 
March 2021 providing for the implementation of the 
Civil Code on ensuring the performance of obligations 
no longer stipulates a mechanism for seizing 
collateral for disposal. Therefore, banks must initiate 
a lawsuit in case a customer does not cooperate in 
the disposal of collateral, resulting in prolonged bad 
debt settlement and depending on the resolution 
procedures of competent courts. In addition, in 2022, 
credit institutions (including BIDV) contributed inputs 
on developing a mechanism to legalize Resolution 
42 on piloting the settlement of bad debts of credit 
institutions - a mechanism for effective debt collection 
for credit institutions in general and BIDV in particular 
that should be documented as law and related 
documents.
Regarding dispute settlement in the fields of civil 
and commercial matters: Basically, the settlement 
of disputes at the court related to credit contracts 
and collateral has ensured the legal and legitimate 
interests of credit institutions. In addition, there still 
remained some cases where BIDV was a bona fide 
mortgagee in accordance with the law (receiving 
collateral based on the certificate of ownership issued 
by a competent authority without any dispute at the 
time of collateral acceptance), the Court still declared 
the mortgage transaction invalid because the previous 
asset transaction with a third party was declared 
invalid. On 2 August 2021, the Supreme People’s Court 
issued Official Letter No. 02/TANDTC-PC addressing 
trial issues. Accordingly, a guideline for judgment was 
directed to the court system with the following content: 
Credit institutions need to carry out procedures for 
appraisal and verification of the asset which serves 
as a basis to prove the actual owner of the asset, 
then a bona fide third party can be identified. This is 
also the point of view that credit institutions should 
pay attention to and learn from in the process of 
establishing new security relationships with customers.
In addition, the Government and the State Bank of 
Vietnam also issued important Decrees and Circulars 
to guide the implementation of the provisions of law 
in the field of finance and banking, including: Decree 
No. 65/2022/ND-CP amending and supplementing 
a number of articles of Decree No. 153/2020/ND-
CP dated 31 December 2020 providing for offering 
and trading private placement corporate bonds in 
the domestic market and offering corporate bonds 
to international markets; Decree No. 99/2022/ND-
CP dated 30 November 2022 on registration of 
security interests; Circular 11/2022/TT-NHNN dated 
30 September 2022 providing for bank guarantees in 
replacement of Circular No. 07/2015/TT-NHNN dated

As a developing economy which has strongly integrated

of banking and finance, the country’s legal system 
on banking is still in the process of being finalized 
to progressively meet the international standards.

the State Bank of Vietnam will continue to promulgate

to the operation of commercial banks in general and 
BIDV in particular. Impacts of the changes in policies 
and laws are unpredictable and beyond the control 
of BIDV. Therefore, this can be considered one of the 
potential risks for investors relating to the changes in

and manage new types of risks. Accordingly, BIDV 
always regularly updates and closely follows the 
economic situation for internal communication, 
proactively implementing measures to respond in an 
appropriate and timely manner, taking early control of 
arising risks to ensure business efficiency against any 
fluctuation in the business environment.

established a system of policies, regulations, appetites

risks according to internal regulations as well as in

always monitored and controlled by BIDV in adherence

policies, regulations, and programs on measuring the

regulations, reputational risk appetite and limits, and 
is developed according to advanced international 
standards and in compliance with internal regulations 
on risk management as well as the State Bank’s 
regulations. The reputational risk management was 
tailored to each unit and individual. Based on the 
reputational risk management policies issued by the

limit reputational risks. In addition to technical tools,

prevent risks. At the same time, BIDV continues to 
periodically review and update policies, regulations, 
measurement methods, and supplement and upgrade 
the reputational risk management and measuring 
systems and programs towards digital transformation 
in order to best meet the regulations of the State Bank 
as well as international practices. 
Information technology (IT) risk is the possibility of 
loss when performing activities related to information 
systems, management and use of hardware, software, 
communication, system interface, operations and 
people.
BIDV has identified IT risk as a material risk independent 
of operational risk and has implemented uniform IT 
risk management activities to ensure compliance with 
regulations of the authorities towards practice and 
actual situation.

risk management, BIDV performed the following tasks:
(i) Continuing to implement the organizational 
structure under the model of 3 lines of defense;

and documents;
(iii) Establishing and monitoring the compliance with IT 
risk appetite and limits;
(iv) 
Officially 
deploying 
independent 
IT 
risk 
management measurement tools such as RCSA (Risk 
Control Self-Assessment), KRI (Key Risk Indicator), 
scorecard, LDC (Loss data collection), using the 
findings of internal and external auditors.
(v) Conducting periodical and ad-hoc reports on IT risk 
management.

and individuals.

investment relations between Vietnam and Laos.

The world economy in 2022 faced many difficulties 
due to the prolonged war between Russia and 
Ukraine, rising inflation, interest rate hikes, tightened 
monetary and fiscal policies and the consequences 
of the Covid-19 pandemic, leading to the slowing 
economic growth. Against that backdrop, under the 
close and timely leadership of the Party; the active 
and close coordination of the National Assembly; the 
drastic direction of the Government; and the active 
and unanimous participation of all levels, sectors, 
localities, business community and people, Vietnam’s 
economy in 2022 achieved positive results: GDP 
growth reached 8.02%; the average consumer price 
index was controlled at 3.15%; total import-export 
turnover reached USD732.5 billion - the highest ever; 
trade surplus was USD11.2 billion.
The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) actively, flexibly and 
synchronously regulated monetary policy instruments, 
contributing to controlling inflation, stabilizing the 
macro-economy, 
and 
supporting 
the 
economic 
recovery, particularly: (i) Flexible regulation of interest 
rates from 23 September 2022, and encouraging 
credit institutions to reduce costs to keep lending 
interest rates stable and reduce interest rates in a 
number of priority areas; (ii) Managing credit towards 
increasing resources and ability to extend credit to 
businesses, subjects, and fields that are in urgent need, 
while ensuring safe and effective growth. As a result, 
credit growth of the whole industry increased 14.5% 
compared to 2021. In addition, the SBV regulated the 
exchange rate appropriately, combining the selling of 
a large amount of foreign currencies to supplement 
the liquidity supply for the market, contributing to 
stabilizing the foreign currency market in the context 
of a strong USD appreciation.

IMPLEMENTATION OF REGULATIONS 
ON CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
BIDV is committed to implementing corporate 
governance in compliance with the provisions of the 
law on corporate governance for large-scale public 
companies and listed companies such as the Law on 
Enterprises, the Law on Credit Institutions, the Law 
on Securities, Circular 116/2020/TT-BTC Guiding a 
number of articles of corporate governance applicable 
to public companies, Circular 96/2020/TT-BTC Guiding 
information disclosure in the market securities, 
BIDV’s Governance Regulations approved by the 
General Meeting of Shareholders and other relevant 
regulations. BIDV has appointed a person in charge of 
corporate governance with full functions and duties as 
prescribed. BIDV is also a state-owned enterprise that 
always ensures to fully comply with the content and 
deadlines for information disclosure in accordance 
with current regulations.
Under the direction of the Board of Directors, in recent 
years, in addition to complying with regulations on 
corporate governance and information disclosure in 
accordance with current laws, BIDV has studied and 
applied the ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard, 
Corporate Governance Code of Conduct according to 
best practices for public companies in Vietnam, jointly 
developed by the State Securities Commission and 
the International Financial Organization (IFC). BIDV 
determines that this is a complete, comprehensive 
and highly practical guide on corporate governance 
for the Bank to gradually apply the best corporate 
governance principles in line with international 
practices. This is both an intrinsic requirement of 
corporate governance at BIDV and the desire of BIDV’s 
shareholders, investors and stakeholders to perfect 
corporate governance in line with the development of 
all aspects of the business, enhance transparency in 
operations, achieve corporate governance standards 
similar to those of enterprises in ASEAN and the world, 
and maintain competitiveness in the long term.
The specific corporate governance objectives of BIDV 
include: (i) ensuring the interests of shareholders, 
investors and related parties; (ii) enhancing publicity 
and transparency in the Bank’s operations; (iii) 
effectively 
operating 
the 
corporate 
governance 
system; (iv) ensuring the effective operation of the 
Board of Directors, Supervisory Board and Board of 
Management.
In order to concretize compliance with the principles 
of corporate governance in practice, BIDV periodically 
evaluates the effectiveness of the Bank’s corporate 
governance system according to the ASEAN Corporate 
Governance Scorecard, based on five aspects: Rights 
of Shareholders; Equitable treatment of Shareholders; 
Role of stakeholders; Disclosure and Transparency; 
Responsibilities of the Board.

SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT REPORT
The world economy in 2022 started with optimistic expectations as the Covid-19 epidemic was 
controlled and many countries moved towards living safely with Covid-19, promoting normalized 
socio-economic activities. International organizations highly appreciate Vietnam’s efforts in recovery, 
macro stability and socio-economic progress, helping to improve the country’s reputation worldwide; 
Vietnam continues to maintain its advantages in attracting foreign investment. Nevertheless, a series 
of issues such as natural disasters, floods, air pollution, and unpredictable climate change continues 
to be one of the risk factors, challenges and impacts on the world economy and the Vietnamese 
economy in particular. This increases challenges and requirements for maintaining sustainable 
development, protecting the environment, saving energy as well as efficient use of natural resources.
In principle, the banking industry has no or insignificant direct impact on the environment. However, 
by granting credit and providing products and services to its vast network of customers, the bank 
indirectly affects sustainable development and the environment.
With a long history of over 65 years, BIDV is currently the leading commercial bank in Vietnam in terms 
of total assets of more than VND2 quadrillion and the number of individual customers accounting 
for 16% of Vietnam’s population, SME customers accounting for 40% of the country’s total number 
of SMEs. In order to develop such a large scale and strong customer base, BIDV always looks for 
solutions to effectively connect our business activities with ensuring the interests of customers, striving 
to bring sustainable values to the community, businesses and partners:
Firstly, recognizing the importance of the bank in 
achieving sustainable development goals in the long 
term, BIDV has built a green development strategy, a 
sustainable financing strategy, promoting green growth 
in our business strategy of 2021-2025 and our vision to 
2030. At the same time, BIDV integrated and updated 
information on the implementation of sustainable 
development at BIDV in our reports, presentations at 
seminars, conferences and meetings with domestic and 
foreign partners. 
Secondly, BIDV has established Sustainable Finance 
Project Management Unit (PMU), performing the 
advisory function for the Board of Directors to research, 
direct, coordinate and organize the implementation of 
tasks related to (i) Sustainable finance implementation 
at BIDV; (ii) ESG risk management in credit activities; 
and (iii) Orient BIDV to become a Net-zero Bank in our 
operations.
Thirdly, BIDV publicly discloses our responsibility for 
sustainable development. In our annual report, BIDV 
always announces sustainable development built in 
accordance with GRI standards and clearly states the 
bank’s responsibilities to the environment, society and 
employees.
Fourthly, , BIDV always focuses on and professionalizes 
the management of environmental and social risks 
through the credit-granting process. BIDV thoroughly 
assesses environmental risks when appraising projects, 
requiring customers to strictly comply with the provisions 
of the law on environmental protection. During the 
project implementation, BIDV regularly monitors and 
manages social environmental risks in parallel with 
the disbursement process; ensuring projects funded by 
BIDV minimize negative impacts on the environment.
Fifthly, BIDV is always a pioneer and active in social 
security work. BIDV’s social security programs target the 
right audience, at the right time with high pervasiveness 
and recognition by the community.
Last but not least, with over 28,000 employees, BIDV 
always determines human resource development in 
both quantity and quality as its core task in business 
strategy and is vital for successfully achieving the set 
goals.
The above-mentioned efforts enhance the position, 
foundation and long-term reputation of BIDV, specifically:
Firstly, sustainable development, in broad, includes 
sustainability in terms of capital-asset structure, 
customer base and financial health is the basis for BIDV 
to satisfy the Basel II requirements, creating a premise 
for the successful implementation of business strategy 
to 2025 and vision to 2030: “Being the leading financial 
institution in the Southeast Asia, which has the best 
digital platform in Vietnam, striving to be among the 
top 100 largest banks in Asia”.
Secondly, developing sustainably not only helps BIDV 
to limit credit risks but also improves BIDV’s reputation, 
recognized by the international communities and trusted 
in cooperation in the context of various changes in the 
Government’s foreign entrusted capital management 
mechanism. BIDV has successfully mobilized capital 
sources from the World Bank for the Renewable Energy 
Project (REDP), the Energy Efficiency Project in Vietnam 
Industry (VEEIE),... In May 2021, BIDV signed a SUNREF 
Credit line of USD100 million with AFD to develop green 
finance without the government guarantee.

image to the social community, shareholders and 
employees for BIDV. In 2022, with various efforts in

orientation of “green bank” to specific actions, BIDV

customer satisfaction index.

Party Committee - Board of Directors - General Director 
issued Joint Resolution No. 636/NQLT-DU-HĐQT-TGD 
approving the contents of BIDV’s cultural handbook. On 
this basis, BIDV’s Board of Directors issued Decision No. 
666/NQ-BIDV issuing BIDV Culture Handbook.
BIDV Culture Handbook fully explains 5 core values, 5 
work ethic standards, and 9 universal codes of conduct 
for employees throughout the system, contributing to 
building awareness for the whole system. leaders and 
employees throughout the system, improving corporate 
culture, forming the standard behavior and working 
style of BIDV staff, and at the same time serving as 
the basis for each individual employee to cultivate and 
practice work ethics and cultured behavior.
In which, 5 core values “Intelligence - Belief - Integrity 
– Detail orientation - Vitality” are formulated into 
“iBIDV”, making it easy to remember and recall. Codes 
of Ethics and Codes of Conduct are made concise and 
memorable with detailed explanations to help staff fully 
understand BIDV’s regulations.
After issuing the handbook, BIDV implemented various 
forms of communication such as issuing both digital 
and printed copies of Cultural Handbook, posters and 
videos, releasing “Fun Office” sitcom series relating 
to the values discussed in the handbook, organizing 
iBIDV writing contest on BIDVZone - an internal social 
network, to encourage staff to study the handbook, etc. 
Additionally, BIDV also added corporate culture content 
to training courses for new staff, future bank leaders, 
trainee managers, etc. Assessment of corporate culture 
compliance became part of staff evaluation. BIDV also 
held an official kick-off event, during which all BIDV 
leaders and staff unanimously signed a commitment to 
comply with BIDV Culture Handbook. 
BIDV’s Board of Directors issued the Decision on the 
establishment and Regulation on organization and 
operation of the Steering Committee for the Prevention 
and Control of Corruption, Negativity and Crime.

Successful organization of Bank-wide Sports Festivals 
Also in 2022, BIDV successfully organized a Sports 
Festival at the system level. 
Before the Finals, 11 Regional Sports Festivals were 
held with the enthusiastic response of grassroots 
trade unions, athletes, coaches, fans, etc. After days 
of exciting matches with noble sportsmanship, all 
11 regions successfully selected excellent athletes to 
compete in the final in 06 following categories: football, 
table tennis, tennis, badminton, tug of war, and running.
There were 951 outstanding athletes competing in the 
Final, representing more than 26,000 union members 
and employees of 245 grassroots trade unions in 11 trade 
union areas in the BIDV system. The addition of the 
running category to BIDV Sports Festival 2022 helped 
attract a large number of athletes and employees, 
creating momentum for the running movement. In the 
spirit of enthusiasm, nobility, honesty and solidarity, 
the teams gave the audience exciting and high quality 
performances. 
BIDV Sports Festival 2022 was a big festival, an 
opportunity for union members and employees to 
exchange and learn from each other, tightening 
solidarity in the system. This event made way to 
evaluate physical training and sports activities of each 
BIDV unit in each region, to gain more knowledge and 
new experiences in directing and building cultural and 
sports activities throughout the system, helping with 
BIDV’s sports movement, strongly motivating union 
members and employees to achieve business success 
in 2022 and the following years. This event also helped 
BIDV spread the positive brand image and culture as 
a socially responsible company to localities and social 
communities through a variety of activities including 
sports and fitness, social security, and charity.

According to Circular 03, the bank should make a 
specific provision for customers whose debts are 
rescheduled, or granted interest and fees exemption or 
reduction as prescribed by this Circular as follows:
	• Up to 31 December 2021: at least 30% of the specific 
provision additionally made;
	• Up to 31 December 2022: at least 60% of the specific 
provision additionally made; and
	• Up to 31 December 2023: 100% of the specific 
provision additionally made.
In accordance with Circular 11, a general provision is 
made for credit losses which are yet to be identified 
during the loan classification and specific provision 
process as well as in cases where the Bank encounters 
potential financial difficulty due to the deterioration 
in loan quality. Accordingly, the Bank is required to 
fully make and maintain a general provision at 0.75% 
of total loans which are classified in groups 1 to 4 as 
at 31 December excluding deposits at domestic credit 
institutions, foreign bank’s branches in Vietnam in 
accordance with law and deposits at foreign credit 
institutions; loans, purchases of valuable papers with 
other credit institutions, foreign banks’ branches 
in Vietnam; purchases of promissory notes, bills, 
certificates of deposit, bonds issued in Vietnam by 
other credit institutions, foreign banks’ branches; and 
repurchase and resale of government bonds according 
to Circular 11.
WRITE-OFF OF BAD DEBTS
Provision is recorded in the consolidated income 
statement as an expense and will be used to write off 
bad debts. According to Circular 11, the Bank must 
set up a Risk Settlement Committee to write off bad 
debts if they are classified in Group 5, or if legal entity 
borrowers are liquidated or bankrupt, or if individual 
borrowers deceased or are missing.
CLASSIFICATION 
OF 
OFF-BALANCE-SHEET 
COMMITMENTS
The Bank classifies guarantee, acceptances of payment 
and unconditional, irrevocable loan commitments 
with specific effective date (collectively referred to 
as “off-balance-sheet commitments”) into groups as 
stipulated in Article 9, Article 10 or Article 11 of Circular 
11. Accordingly, off-balance-sheet commitments are 
classified by risk level as follows: Standard, Special 
mention, Substandard, Doubtful and Loss. 
(continued)
Interest and similar income/expenses
Interest income and interest expenses are recognized 
in the consolidated income statement on the accrual 
basis. The accrued interest income arising from the 
loans that are classified from group 2 to group 5 in 
accordance with Circular 11, accrued interest income 
on loans restructured and maintained in Standard 
loan group (group 1) as prescribed in Circular 01 and 
Decree No. 55/2015/ND-CP of 9 June 2015 will not 
be recognized in the consolidated income statement. 
Accrued interest income on such loans is recorded as 
an off-balance-sheet item and is recognized in the 
consolidated income statement when it is actually 
received.
Interest income and interest expenses on investments 
in securities are recorded on the accrual basis. 
Accrued interest income of overdue securities is not 
recognized in the consolidated income statement for 
the year. Accrued interest income on such investments 
is recorded as an off-balance-sheet item and is only 
recognized in the consolidated income statement 
when it is actually received.
REVENUE AND EXPENSES
Insurance incomes and expenses
Direct premiums are recognized in accordance with 
Circular No. 50/2017/TT-BTC by the Ministry of Finance 
effective 01 July 2017 (Circular 50). Accordingly, direct 
premium income is recognized when the following 
conditions are met: (1) the agreement has been entered 
into by the insurer and the insured, who has paid 
premiums fully; (2) there is evidence that the insurance 
policy has been signed and the insured has paid the 
premiums fully; and (3) the insurance policy is signed 
and there is an agreement between the insurer and the 
insured for delayed payment of insurance premium, 
and in this case, the insurer will still record the premium 
amount as an income for the current year even though 
the amount has not been paid by the insured. The 
payment period is no longer than 30 days from the 
effective date of the insurance policy. 
In the case of the periodic payment, the insurer records 
income from insurance premiums of the first payment 
period when the contract is effective and only records 
revenue from insurance premiums of the next payment 
periods when the insured has fully paid the insurance 
premium as contract agreements. In case the insured 
has not fully paid the insurance premium according 
to the payment term, the insurance contract is 
automatically terminated at the end of the insurance 
premium payment term. The prepaid premium before 
the due date as at the consolidated balance sheet date 
is recognized in the “Other payables and liabilities” 
item in the consolidated balance sheet. 
Insurance claim expenses are recognized when the 
claim documents are completed and approved by the 
authorized person. In case that the final claim amount 
has not been finalized, but the insurer is certain that 
the loss is within its insured liabilities and has paid an 
advance to the customer as per their request, such 
advance would also be recognized as claim expense. 
The claims which have not been approved as at the 
consolidated balance sheet date are considered as 
outstanding claims and included in claim reserves.
The commission expense of each product is calculated 
as a percentage of the direct premium as stated in 
Circular 50. Commission expenses are allocated and 
recognized in the consolidated income statement 
corresponding with the premium earned.
Income from service charges and commissions
Income from service charges and commissions is 
recognized on an accrual basis.
Income from guarantee and L/C commitment activities
Income from guarantee and L/C commitment activities 
is recognized on the accrual and allocation basis. 
Recognition of dividends and profits received
Cash dividends and profits received from investment 
and capital contribution activities are recorded in the 
consolidated income statement when the Bank’s right 
to receive dividends and profits has been established. 
Share dividends, which are distributed from profits of 
joint stock companies, are recognized neither as an 
increase in the value of received shares nor financial 
income in the consolidated financial statements but 
are only used for tracking the increase in the number 
of shares according to Circular No. 22/2017/TT-NHNN 
dated 29 December 2017 issued by the State Bank of 
Vietnam.
Revenue from other service provision
When the contract results can be determined reliably, 
revenue will be recorded based on the level of work 
completion. If the contract outcome cannot be 
determined reliably, revenue will only be recognized at 
the recoverable level of recorded expenses.

Post-employment benefits
Post-employment benefits are paid to retired employees 
of the Bank and its subsidiaries in Vietnam by the 
Social Insurance Agency under the Ministry of Labor, 
Invalids and Social Affairs. The Bank and its subsidiaries 
in Vietnam are required to contribute to these post-
employment benefits by paying a social insurance 
premium to the Social Insurance Agency at the rate of 
17.5% of an employee’s monthly salary for their working 
period. In addition, the Bank also uses its Welfare Fund to 
pay one-time retirement benefits to employees under the 
Bank’s regulations.
Severance allowance 
According to Article 46 of Labor Code 2019, the Bank 
and its subsidiaries in Vietnam are responsible to pay 
severance allowance for employees who have regularly 
worked at the Bank and its subsidiaries for 12 months 
or more, half-month salary allowance for each working 
year before 01 January 2009. The working period used for 
calculation of severance allowance excludes the period 
that employees benefit from unemployment insurance 
and the working period that employees receive severance 
allowance, retrenchment benefits from employers.
Retrenchment benefits
According to Article 47 of Labor Code 2019, the Bank 
and its subsidiaries in Vietnam are responsible to pay 
retrenchment benefits for employees who have regularly 
worked at the Bank and its subsidiaries for 12 months 
or more but are retrenched from their jobs as a result 
of organizational restructuring, technological changes, 
economic reasons, business combination, consolidation 
and split. For each year of employment, the employee is 
entitled to one-month salary but not less than two times 
the average salary of 06 consecutive months immediately 
preceding the job loss date. The working period used for 
calculation of retrenchment benefits excludes the period

that employees benefit from unemployment insurance 
and the working period that employees receive severance 
allowance, retrenchment benefits from employers.
Unemployment insurance 
According to the Circular No. 28/2015/TT-BLDTBXH 
dated 31 July 2015 of the Ministry of Labor - War Invalids 
and Social Affairs guiding the implementation of Article 
52 of the Employment Law 2013 and the Decree No. 
28/2015/ND-CP of the Government dated 12 March 
2015 regulating the implementation of the Law on 
unemployment insurance, from 01 January 2009, the Bank 
and its subsidiaries are obliged to pay unemployment 
insurance to eligible employees at 1% of their salary fund 
allocated for unemployment insurance.
